Revised assessment: The FOMC communicates significant near-term downside risks from COVID-19 and pairs an ELB rate cut with large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repos, discount-window easing, and dollar swap lines to stabilize funding—responses aligned with the literature on the zero lower bound and policy rules (Taylor rule prescriptions; Eggertsson/Woodford on ZLB and commitment tools), and with financial accelerator dynamics (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist) that argue for aggressive liquidity support. Evidence on QE and forward guidance reducing term premia and supporting market functioning (e.g., Rudebusch–Wu; Romer and Romer narrative identification) further supports the Fed’s approach. Net tone remains cautious/negative due to the shock (“will weigh on economic activity … and pose risks”), but is tempered by decisive policy action.
